Bukayo Saka’s hat-trick helped England secure their best men's FIFA World Cup finish since 1966 with a 6-4 win over France in an exhilarating bronze medal match.
Saka’s brace opened up a remarkable 4-0 half-time lead but France roared back through Kylian Mbappe’s double either side of Bradley Barcola’s strike.
England re-established a cushion when Saka completed his treble from the spot and though Ousmane Dembele set up a nervy finale, Jude Bellingham finally made the outcome safe with a brilliant solo goal as the Three Lions ended a memorable tournament on a high.
Dean Henderson kept out Rayan Cherki as France sought a response but England continued to look dangerous and were denied a second when Saka’s fine finish from an angle was ruled out for offside.
And Rashford was key as England trebled their lead. He raced on to Saka’s through ball and saw his effort kept out by Maignan, before keeping his composure to set up the Arsenal man to find the net.
Rashford almost set up Ivan Toney for another and the fourth was not long in coming. Eberechi Eze played an inch-perfect through ball to his clubmate and Saka took a touch out of his feet before converting past Maignan into the bottom corner.
England’s nerves were finally settled when an overlapping Djed Spence was fouled by Malo Gusto and Saka stepped up to coolly convert, becoming the fourth England player to score a hat-trick at a men’s World Cup, following in the footsteps of Sir Geoff Hurst, Gary Lineker and Harry Kane.
